comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Use decision: CUA for bar within restaurant withdrawn after 5 months, 66 m away on Valencia St. While the record does not state why, the withdrawal of a bar-related CUA on the same block signals that discretionary bar approvals can face obstacles in NCT-VALENCIA, though the specific circumstances are unknown.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at 1007-1017 Valencia St (45 m away, NCT-VALENCIA) for continuation of existing Type 41 license. Approved 2008 with explicit note: 'Approval does not establish a new bar use at subject location.' Directly relevant to the distinction between restaurant and bar uses.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved with emphasis that Type 41 continuation does not create a bar use. This underscores that changing from the existing Type 41 restaurant at 995 Valencia to a bar use (even retaining Type 41 or transferring a Type 42 under SUD rules) will be treated as a change of use requiring CUA, not a continuation.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Active Place of Entertainment permit at 998 Valencia St (31 m away, Amados), the closest entertainment permit to the subject site. Demonstrates that POE permits for live music venues operate successfully on this block.

Establishes that live amplified entertainment is permitted and operating immediately adjacent to the site, strongly supporting feasibility of a POE permit for the proposed concept's live music component.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at 998 Valencia St (52 m away, NCT-VALENCIA) approved POE permit as accessory to existing retail use in 2014, subject to Police Code limits (≤1/3 gross floor area). Same property as the active Amados POE permit.

Establishes precedent for entertainment permits on this block when structured as accessory to a principal use, though the proposed bar concept would make entertainment and alcohol service co-equal rather than accessory.

The withdrawal of a CUA for a concept blending food, beer/wine, and live entertainment suggests discretionary approvals for entertainment-heavy uses face uncertainty even when structured as eating places rather than bars, though the withdrawal reason is not stated.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at 1101 Valencia St (214 m away, NCT-VALENCIA) approved continuation of existing bar license in 2006 with condition prohibiting expansion of square footage or substantial change in mode or character. comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved with strict no-expansion condition, citing prohibition on expanding establishments selling alcoholic beverages. Even continuations of existing bar uses in NCT-VALENCIA were conditioned against expansion or character changes, signaling heightened scrutiny of alcohol uses in this corridor under the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD.

filing_playbook.action: Contact SF Planning Department Zoning Information Counter or file a Zoning Letter of Determination request to confirm in writing that a Type 42 license transferred from a bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD satisfies Planning Code § 249.60 for a bar CUA at 995 Valencia St.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the concept is a beer-and-wine bar (Planning Code § 102) with limited kitchen and live music, closing at 1 am, and that you intend to transfer a Type 42 or Type 48 license from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD as required by § 249.60. Ask whether that satisfies the SUD requirement and whether any additional findings or conditions apply. Request the answer in writing before purchasing or escrowing any license.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a California ABC license broker with Mission SUD experience to identify available Type 42 licenses held by bars within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, and confirm transfer price, escrow process, and timing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Specify that the license must be held by a bar (not a restaurant or other use) currently operating within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD boundaries, and that the transfer will be to 995 Valencia St in the same SUD. Ask the broker to provide a list of available licenses, their current addresses, asking prices, and estimated escrow and ABC transfer timeline. Do not enter escrow until the Zoning Letter confirms the transfer satisfies § 249.60.

timeline_cost.notes: Minimum 8–9 months (240–270 days) if the CUA, POE, ABC transfer, and building permit proceed in parallel without appeals or denials: CUA 120 days, POE 45 days (filed after CUA approval), ABC transfer 60 days (filed after CUA and building permit are approved), building permit 60 days (plan review in parallel with CUA), DPH plan check and inspection 60 days (routed with building permit). Maximum 19 months (570 days) if the CUA or POE permit is appealed (add 30–90 days), the ABC transfer is protested or requires a PCN finding (add 60–120 days), or the building permit is delayed by incomplete plans or DPH/Fire corrections (add 60 days). Government costs: CUA $3,100 (base fee, no construction), POE $2,708, ABC Type 42 transfer $1,000–$1,600, DPH plan check $828–$1,241, DPH Health Permit $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (varies with construction valuation), plus SF business registration $55–$95, CA entity formation $70, seller's permit $0, EIN $0, food safety manager cert $100–$250, RBS training for staff ~$100–$200 total, ASCAP/BMI licenses ~$600–$5,000/year. The license transfer price (typically $0 for a Type 42 transferred from a closing bar, but brokers may charge $5,000–$20,000 depending on market availability within the Mission SUD) is not included in government costs. The critical path is the CUA hearing (4–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, and hearing scheduling), followed by the ABC license transfer (2–5 months depending on protests and PCN process). Construction can begin after the building permit is issued, but the Health Permit and ABC license must be in hand before opening to the public.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA district where bars require Conditional Use Authorization, and the address falls within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§249.60), which mandates that any new or relocated bar must use a Type 42 or 48 license transferred from another bar within the SUD. The records show an active Type 41 license (on-sale beer and wine, eating place) at 995 Valencia St issued in 2023 to Sarita's Grill & Beer, establishing the current use as a Restaurant. Changing from Restaurant to Bar triggers a change of use requiring CUA. The immediate area is saturated: 24 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 9 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, and 61 licenses within 1,000 ft—a density that will likely trigger ABC's undue concentration review and require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the City. Too few comparable dated use decisions exist within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years (only 3 total: 1 approved, 2 withdrawn) to establish an approval rate, but nearby entertainment permits are active (Amados at 998 Valencia has a POE permit, Hidden Frequency at 2500 Mission has POE + Extended Hours).
